runs.summary: Data through Sep 4 (Q3 partial). Top 3: SMH +57.4%, XLE +45.2%, XBI +34.5%. SPY P/E: 26.11x (down from 28.00x)
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: SMH +57.4% (P/E 42.40x, Expensive), XLE +45.2% (16.37x, Fair), XBI +34.5% (P/E N/A), CIBR +32.7% (37.26x, Expensive), XLK +30.4% (37.35x, Expensive).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XLC -4.3% (16.54x, Fair), XLY -3.4% (26.66x, Elevated), XLU +2.3% (20.31x, Fair), JETS +2.6% (10.13x, Cheap), GLD +2.6% (P/E N/A).

Notable shifts: a sharp valuation reset this run — all 23 tracked sector P/E figures moved (almost all lower), a reversal from the prior run's universal stability, and the SPY reference multiple fell from 28.00x to 26.11x. That drove the tracker's only valuation band crossing: MLPs/Pipelines (AMLP) moved Fair→Cheap (16.69x→13.91x). On performance, Cybersecurity (CIBR) gave back much of its earlier sharp reacceleration — Q3 partial fell from +9.7% to +5.3%, pulling YTD down from +38.3% to +32.7%, the tracker's largest decliner. Semiconductors (SMH) and Energy (XLE) both extended their leads, with SMH overtaking XLE for the tracker's top 2026 spot (+57.4% YTD) as its Q3 drawdown eased. Consumer Discretionary (XLY) and Communication Services (XLC) remain the tracker's only two negative-YTD sectors, both drifting further underwater.

runs.summary: Data through Aug 28 (Q3 partial). Top 3: SMH +53.6%, XLE +42.1%, CIBR +38.3%. SPY P/E: 28.00x (unchanged)
runs.content:
Top 5 YTD 2026: SMH +53.6% (P/E 44.89x, Expensive), XLE +42.1% (20.02x, Fair), CIBR +38.3% (38.16x, Expensive), XBI +33.3% (P/E N/A), XLK +29.3% (39.32x, Expensive).

Bottom 5 YTD 2026: XLC -3.5% (15.50x, Fair), XLY -1.5% (30.94x, Elevated), XLU +1.4% (21.64x, Fair), XRT +2.4% (15.65x, Fair), GLD +3.2% (P/E N/A).

Notable shifts: all 25 sector P/E figures came back unchanged from the prior run — a stable read with zero valuation band crossings, versus four last run. Performance-wise, a broad, mild two-day pullback (Aug 26→28) hit 20 of 25 sectors' Q3 partials and YTD figures, consistent with a short risk-off move. The clear exception was Cybersecurity (CIBR), which reaccelerated sharply — Q3 partial more than doubled from +4.2% to +9.7%, lifting YTD from +31.4% to +38.3%, the tracker's best two-day mover by far. Energy (XLE) and Technology (XLK) also bucked the pullback, both improving slightly. Consumer Discretionary (XLY) and Communication Services (XLC) remain the tracker's only two negative-YTD sectors, both little changed.
